applies_to: CAREL k.air mini and k.air large air handling unit controllers (the versions with BACnet IP and BACnet MS/TP); k.air smart is Modbus only.
summary: k.air is CAREL's ready-made air handling unit controller. Its manual has a supervisor variable table with a Modbus address and a BACnet object for every variable: about 4,350 objects covering BMS commands, setpoints, every sensor and output (with its configuration), fan, humidifier, compressor and heat recovery data, and one alarm BV per alarm. Most of the list is configuration; an integrator normally maps a small part of it.
notes: The table gives Modbus classes, not a BACnet access column. Access here follows the Modbus class: coils and holding registers W, discrete inputs and input registers R.
Object names are the CAREL variable names from the table. No engineering units are printed; descriptions carry the Modbus address, value meanings, and a 32-bit flag for Dim 2 variables.

Repeated rows in the source were dropped (CS112, DI1159, HR614/615, IR118/119, IR626-632). On page 136 the source repeats 12 rows from page 133 (DI340-DI366) between wrapped variable names; those repeats were dropped and the wrapped names joined.

One printed instance clash is kept as printed: BV 1436 (DI1210) for two ZA return fan alarms. The CoilRegOffset row on page 144 is garbled (it repeats HR143/PIV1666 and PIV1667 from the previous page next to HR192/AV1715); it is listed as AV 1715 (Modbus HR192), which fits the table's sequence. OA_CoilActMode is printed as PI4577 and listed as PIV 4577.
The supervisor table skips some Modbus addresses; a few objects (for example AV 3436) appear only in the manual's parameter tables and are not in this list.
Which serial or Ethernet port speaks BACnet is set in menu Y (BMS Line or BMS2 Line = BACnet MS/TP, Ethernet 2 Line = BACnet IP).

source.title: k.air - Air handling unit controller, user manual (11. Supervisor variable table)

integration.summary: Enable BMS on/off with BV 234, then switch the unit with BV 2 and select summer or winter with BV 4. Write the comfort temperature setpoints (AV 2585 winter, AV 2584 summer) if the BMS owns them. Read the unit status (PIV 3645), the supply, return and room temperatures, and the generic alarm BV 902; BV 1 resets alarms. Configure the BMS offline alarm (PIV 2898/2899) if the BMS should be supervised.

minimum_points.why: Must be on for the BMS on/off command to work

minimum_points.name: Scheduler_OnOffUnit.BMS_OnOff
minimum_points.why: Unit on/off command from the BMS

minimum_points.name: SchedStatus
minimum_points.why: Active status: 0 off, 1 economy, 2 pre-comfort, 3 comfort

integration.enable: The unit can be switched by keypad/th-Tune, BMS, digital input and scheduler; any enabled source set to off stops it. BMS on/off works only when BV 234 (enable on/off request by BMS) is on; BV 2 then turns the unit on or off.
integration.heartbeat: PIV 2898 selects BMS offline handling (0 disabled, 1 warning only, 2 alarm, 3 alarm with timeout) and PIV 2899 sets the timeout, 120 s by default. BV 1347 shows the BMS offline alarm.
setup: Choose the BACnet port in menu Y: BMS Line or BMS2 Line = 2 (BACnet MS/TP on RS485) or Ethernet 2 Line = 1 (BACnet IP).
Y003 sets the BACnet device instance (also the MS/TP station address); baud rate, parity and stop bits are in menu Y too.
gotchas: Most of the ~4,350 objects are I/O configuration (board, channel, probe type, limits); writing them changes the unit's set-up.
Setpoints exist per season and per mode (economy, pre-comfort, comfort); the current setpoint values are read-only status objects.
Object instances are not derived from the Modbus address; use the table, not a formula.
